# Configuration reference

Every setting you can change without editing code: launcher environment variables, the
thermal guard's thresholds, and the switches added to the three patched programs. Defaults
are what runs today. For files on disk (config and state paths) see
[project_architecture.md](architecture.md#configuration-and-state-the-schema).

## GPU detection and program lookup (`scripts/detect-gpu.sh`, `lib/raytube-env.sh`)

Every launcher sources `lib/raytube-env.sh`, which loads `~/.config/raytube/gpu.env` (written by
`scripts/detect-gpu.sh`, run by `install.sh` or on first use) and finds the patched programs.

| Variable | How it's set | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RAYTUBE_RENDER_NODE` | first `i915`/`xe` render node | VA-API device for encoding (this laptop: `/dev/dri/renderD129`) |
| `WF_FORCE_DMABUF` | 1 when the encode GPU isn't the one driving the display | zero-copy capture across GPUs |
| `WF_IMPLICIT_MODIFIER` | 1 when the display GPU is AMD GCN 1.0 (Southern Islands PCI IDs) | implicit-modifier buffers (this laptop's R9 M370X) |
| `RAYTUBE_GPU_ENV` | default `~/.config/raytube/gpu.env` | where the detection result lives |
| `WF_RECORDER_BIN`, `DOUBLETAKE_BIN`, `OMACAST_BIN`, `OMACASTD_BIN` | override, else `build/bin/`, else `project-references/` clones, else PATH | the patched programs |
| `TARGET` | required by `cast-tv.sh` (no built-in default) | the Apple TV's IP; `raytube-cast` sets it |
| `RAYTUBE_LAPTOP_OUTPUT` | unset → first non-TV monitor | where windows come home to |

## Receiver discovery and pairing

`raytube-cast list` asks Avahi for `_airplay._tcp` and `_googlecast._tcp` services and prints
`name<TAB>ip<TAB>paired|unpaired<TAB>airplay|cast`.

- **AirPlay names** come from the mDNS instance name; **Chromecast names** from the TXT `fn=`
  field, which is what `omacast start --to` matches on.
- **A device that speaks both protocols** (the LG "Computer Monitor") is listed once, as
  AirPlay: any Cast entry whose IP already appeared in the AirPlay list is skipped.
- **Paired** means the AirPlay `deviceid` TXT value appears in
  `~/.config/doubletake/credentials.json`. Chromecasts need no pairing and are always `paired`.
- **First connection to an unpaired AirPlay receiver** opens a terminal running `cast-tv.sh`
  instead of the background unit, so the PIN shown on the TV can be typed. After that the
  credential is saved and the Display menu works for that receiver.

## Launcher settings (`cast-tv.sh`)

Short names read by the AirPlay launcher; `raytube-cast start` sets some of them per session
with `systemd-run --setenv` (`TARGET`, `CANVAS`, `AUDIO_DELAY_MS`, `AUDIO_DELAY_FILE`, and in
desktop mode `WF_ARGS`, `PULSE_PROPS`, `DOUBLETAKE_NO_PAD=1`). Each feeds the patched doubletake.
The defaults below apply when `cast-tv.sh` runs by hand (or in the pairing terminal).

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `TARGET` | `<apple-tv-ip>` | Receiver IP (the Office TV) |
| `FPS` | `30` | Capture and encode frame rate |
| `BITRATE` | `20000` | Average kbps; peaks may reach twice this |
| `LATENCY_MS` | `110` | `-target-latency-ms`: playout lead requested from the Apple TV |
| `CANVAS` | `3200x1800` | Encoded canvas (→ `DOUBLETAKE_CANVAS`). `raytube-cast` always sets it to the TV's picture size (`~/.config/raytube/airplay-size/<ip>`, default `1920x1080`) in both modes; the 3200x1800 default is only left for hand runs |
| `WF_RECORDER` | `references/wf-recorder/build/wf-recorder` | Patched wf-recorder; set empty to use the legacy portal path |
| `WF_ARGS` | `-D` | Extra wf-recorder arguments (→ `DOUBLETAKE_WF_ARGS`); desktop mode adds `-o TV` |
| `WF_MAX_FAILURES` | `60` | Screencopy failures tolerated, with backoff, before capture exits |
| `PULSE_PROPS` | `buffer-time=60000 latency-time=20000` | pulsesrc properties (→ `DOUBLETAKE_PULSE_PROPS`); desktop mode adds `device=raytube_tv.monitor` |
| `PW_PROPS` | `min-buffers=8` | pipewiresrc properties, legacy portal path only |
| `NO_COMPOSITOR` | `1` | Skip the GStreamer forced-live compositor, legacy portal path only |
| `AUDIO_DELAY_MS` | `0` | Sound delay in ms (→ `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_MS`); `raytube-cast` passes the TV's saved value |
| `AUDIO_DELAY_FILE` | empty | File re-read live for the delay (→ `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_FILE`); `raytube-cast` passes `~/.config/raytube/av-delay/<ip>` |
| `CAST_GUARD_LOG` | `~/.local/state/raytube/thermal.log` | Read after an exit to tell a thermal ABORT (stop) from a stream error (restart) |

Example: `FPS=24 BITRATE=12000 LATENCY_MS=150 ./cast-tv.sh`.

## Thermal guard settings (`cast-guard.sh`)

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `THROTTLE_C` | `85` | Cap the CPU after 3 samples at or above this (°C) |
| `RECOVER_C` | `78` | Lift the cap at or below this, once `HOLD_S` has passed |
| `ABORT_C` | `92` | Stop the cast after 2 consecutive samples at or above this; one sample at `ABORT_C − 4` throttles at once |
| `THROTTLE_PCT` | `60` | `intel_pstate` `max_perf_pct` while capped |
| `HOLD_S` | `30` | Minimum seconds the cap stays on |
| `INTERVAL` | `2` | Seconds between temperature samples |
| `FAN_MODE` | `quiet` | `quiet`: our own fan curve (the Mac runs these fans flat out from ~67°C); `auto`: SMC control, boost when hot; `max`: maximum for the whole run |
| `CAST_GUARD_SUDO` | `0` | `1` = if the `raytube` group can't write a control yet, try `sudo -n` (opt-in; needs passwordless sudo), e.g. `systemctl --user set-environment CAST_GUARD_SUDO=1` until your next login |
| `TURBO` | `0` | `0` turns Intel turbo boost off for the cast (`intel_pstate/no_turbo`, restored on exit); `1` keeps it |
| `QUIET_RPM` | `3500` | Quiet curve speed up to `QUIET_FROM_C` |
| `QUIET_FROM_C` | `70` | Curve rises linearly above this… |
| `QUIET_MAX_C` | `82` | …to full speed here; at or above it the SMC takes over |
| `QUIET_RESUME_C` | `76` | Curve resumes after `FAN_HOLD_S` at or below this |
| `FAN_BOOST_C` | `80` | `auto` and `quiet` modes: raise fan minimums to maximum at or above this (single samples) |
| `FAN_CALM_C` | `70` | Release them after `FAN_HOLD_S` at or below this |
| `FAN_HOLD_S` | `60` | Seconds of calm before releasing the fans |
| `CAST_GUARD_LOG` | `~/.local/state/raytube/thermal.log` | Where samples and THROTTLE/ABORT events are written |

The quiet curve follows the average of the last 5 samples (~10 s), so a single turbo spike
does not hand the fans to the SMC; throttle and abort still act on every sample.

`CAST_GUARDED=1` is set by `cast-chromecast.sh` when it re-executes itself under the guard, so
it does not wrap itself twice. It is internal; don't set it by hand.

## Chromecast launcher and self-test

- **`cast-chromecast.sh <name>`** always starts a fresh `omacastd`, so the session's
  environment (`RAYTUBE_OUTPUT`, `OMACAST_AUDIO_MONITOR`) applies. It exits 0 on Ctrl+C or a
  unit stop, and 1 if the session ends by itself.
- **`cc-selftest.sh [seconds]`** reads `DEVICE` (default `Chromecast HD`) and `EVENT_LOG`
  (default `0`; `1` asks for the receiver event log, which this firmware rejects).

## Capture (`wf-capture.sh`)

omacast's `video_command`, called as `wf-capture.sh {width} {height} {fps} {kbps}` with
values taken from the same quality settings as the OFFER.

- **`RAYTUBE_OUTPUT`**: the monitor to capture. `raytube-cast` sets it to `TV` in desktop
  mode; unset means the laptop screen.
- **Encoder settings**: `h264_vaapi` on `/dev/dri/renderD129`, VBR at `{kbps}` with the same
  maxrate, GOP `g=15` (a keyframe every 0.5 s at 30 fps, so receivers recover quickly from
  loss), no B-frames, access-unit delimiters, `async_depth=1`.
- **Filter chain**: fit to the canvas with `scale_vaapi`, pad in RGB, then convert to NV12, so
  the bars are black rather than green.

## TV desktop (`raytube-tv`)

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `RAYTUBE_LAPTOP_OUTPUT` | `eDP-1` | The output that windows return to on `send`, `back` and `down` |
| `RAYTUBE_NOTIFY` | unset | `1` shows a brief notification per command; the hotkeys set it (`raytube-tv key` sets it itself) |
| `XDG_STATE_HOME` | `~/.local/state` | Where `raytube-tv up` reads `display-flip`: state `2` places the TV below the laptop (`auto-center-down`) instead of above (`auto-center-up`), the same rule as `monitors.lua` |

The scene list and rotation times live in `~/.config/raytube/tv.json` (see
[tv-desktop.md](tv-desktop.md#scenes)).

## Watchdogs (`cast-watch.sh`, `sync-watch.sh`)

`raytube-cast start` starts `cast-watch.sh` (transient unit `raytube-watch`) if it isn't running, so
it returns after a reboot with the first cast. `sync-watch.sh` is started by hand when needed, e.g.
`systemd-run --user --unit=raytube-syncwatch $PWD/sync-watch.sh` (needs a `-debug` cast).

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `CAST_WATCH_LOG` | `~/.local/state/raytube/cast-watch.log` | `cast-watch.sh` log |
| `SYNC_WATCH_LOG` | `~/.local/state/raytube/sync-watch.log` | `sync-watch.sh` log |

`cast-watch.sh` thresholds are fixed in the script: xruns read every 5 s from `pw-top`; more
than 2 in 30 s raises the cycle to 2048 samples; after a glitch burst or an audio-only capture
restart it runs `raytube-cast resync` once 10 s are calm, at most every 5 minutes.

## Switches in the patched programs

Each switch lives in the matching file under `patches/`.

### doubletake

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DOUBLETAKE_WF_RECORDER` | unset | Path to the patched wf-recorder. When set, capture skips the portal and PipeWire |
| `DOUBLETAKE_WF_ARGS` | unset | Extra wf-recorder arguments |
| `DOUBLETAKE_CANVAS` | receiver's nominal size | Encoded canvas `WxH` |
| `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_MS` | `0` | Shift audio timestamps later by this many ms (0–2000) to match the TV's extra picture delay |
| `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_FILE` | unset | File holding the delay in ms, re-read every 500 ms for live tuning (`~/.config/raytube/av-delay/<ip>`) |
| `DOUBLETAKE_NO_PAD` | unset | `1` skips the pad pass when the captured output already is the canvas size (raytube-cast sets it in desktop mode): saves ~25% capture CPU and ~20% dropped frames |
| `DOUBLETAKE_PULSE_PROPS` | unset | Extra pulsesrc properties; the last `device=` wins |
| `DOUBLETAKE_VAAPI_DEVICE` | first `i915` render node | VA-API device for Intel encoding |
| `DOUBLETAKE_FFMPEG_ASYNC_DEPTH` | `1` | Frames the Intel encoder may hold in flight (ffmpeg's own default is 2) |
| `DOUBLETAKE_NO_COMPOSITOR` | unset | Legacy path: drop the forced-live compositor, which repeats stale frames |
| `DOUBLETAKE_NO_VAPOSTPROC` | unset | Legacy path: skip `vapostproc` (the AMD VA device cannot handle the capture size) |
| `DOUBLETAKE_GL_CONVERT` | unset | Legacy path: colour conversion with a GL shader instead of `videoconvert` |
| `DOUBLETAKE_PW_PROPS` | unset | Legacy path: extra pipewiresrc properties |

### wf-recorder

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `WF_FORCE_DMABUF` | unset | Keep DMA-BUF capture when the encode GPU differs from the compositor's |
| `WF_IMPLICIT_MODIFIER` | unset | Advertise the linear buffer with `DRM_FORMAT_MOD_INVALID`; GCN 1.0 rejects explicit LINEAR |
| `WF_MAX_FAILURES` | `16` (upstream) | Copy failures tolerated; above 16 it also backs off up to 200 ms between retries |
| `WF_ALLOC_DEVICE` | encode device | Allocate capture buffers on another GPU. Tested with the AMD card: no gain |
| `WF_DEBUG_BO` | unset | Log each capture buffer's size, fourcc, modifier and stride |
| `WF_REPEAT_FRAMES` | unset | With `-B`: re-encode the last frame when the compositor sends none for one frame interval (for receivers that show a frame only when the next arrives). Built 2026-09-26, off: the TV desktop already gets 18–27 fps |
| `WF_DEBUG_REPEAT` | unset | Log the first capture timestamps and a repeat count (debugging `WF_REPEAT_FRAMES`) |

### omacast

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `OMACAST_AUDIO_MONITOR` | default sink's monitor | Audio source; desktop mode uses `raytube_tv.monitor` |
| `OMACAST_SETTLE_MS` | `300` | Wait after the mirroring app launches before sending the OFFER, multiplied by the attempt number |
| `OMACAST_OFFER_ATTEMPTS` | `4` | OFFER attempts, each relaunching the app |
| `OMACAST_RTCP_EVENT_LOG` | `0` | `1` requests the receiver event log; Chromecast HD firmware 3.72 rejects that OFFER |

## Per-TV settings and state (AirPlay)

| Path | Written by | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.config/raytube/airplay-size/<ip>` | `raytube-cast size`, Display menu 720p/1080p/1440p | Picture size sent in both modes (absent = `1920x1080`; no file exists today, so the Office TV gets 1080p) |
| `~/.config/raytube/av-delay/<ip>` | `raytube-cast av-delay[-step]`, Display menu Sound sync (50 ms steps, 0–2000) | Sound delay in ms, re-read live by doubletake (`DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_FILE`); Office TV `50` |
| `~/.local/state/raytube/tv-size` | `raytube-tv up` | TV-desktop size, read by `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua` so a reload keeps it |
| PipeWire `settings` metadata `clock.force-quantum` | `raytube-cast` (1024 on start, cleared on stop), `cast-watch.sh` (2048 on glitches) | Audio cycle while casting |
| `~/.local/state/raytube/cast-watch.log` | `cast-watch.sh` (unit `raytube-watch`, `CAST_WATCH_LOG`) | Cast errors, audio stalls and xruns with CPU/temperature context |
| `~/.local/state/raytube/sync-watch.log` | `sync-watch.sh` (unit `raytube-syncwatch`, `SYNC_WATCH_LOG`) | Per-minute fps / source age / slack; needs the cast running with `-debug` |

## Reference repositories (`project-references/`)

| Repo | Role |
|---|---|
| `doubletake`, `wf-recorder`, `omacast` | Patched and built; changes live in `patches/` |
| `openscreen` | Google's Cast Streaming reference; source of the SSRC ranges and the SR ordering fix |
| `pychromecast`, `catt`, `go-chromecast`, `gnome-network-displays`, `fluxcast` | Chromecast senders studied for the approach; URL/HLS casting was rejected for latency |
| `pyatv`, `UxPlay`, `ap2-sender`, `wlroots-airplay-screen-mirror` | AirPlay research clones; not used at runtime |

`references/` is a symlink to `project-references/` kept for older paths.
